purpose: Sorafenib is used to treat certain types of cancer, including kidney cancer, liver cancer, and a type of thyroid cancer. It helps slow or stop the growth of cancer cells and can help shrink tumors. Your doctor has prescribed this because it targets specific pathways that cancer uses to grow and spread.
how_it_works: Cancer cells need certain signals to grow and they also need new blood vessels to feed them. Sorafenib works by blocking the signals inside cancer cells that tell them to keep multiplying. It also cuts off the blood supply that tumors need to grow, essentially starving the cancer cells.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include hand-foot syndrome, which causes redness, soreness, swelling, or blisters on your palms and the soles of your feet. You may also experience diarrhea, fatigue, rash, nausea, hair thinning, high blood pressure, and loss of appetite. Let your care team know if any of these bother you, as there are ways to manage them.
warnings: Sorafenib can cause serious bleeding, so tell your doctor right away if you notice unusual bleeding anywhere. It can raise your blood pressure, so your blood pressure will be monitored regularly. There is a small risk of heart problems and wound healing issues, so tell your doctor if you are planning any surgery. Do not take this medication if you are pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby. Avoid grapefruit while taking this medicine. Always tell all your doctors and pharmacist about every medication and supplement you take, as sorafenib can interact with many drugs.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 400 mg (two 200 mg tablets) taken by mouth twice a day, about 12 hours apart. It is best taken on an empty stomach or with a low-fat meal. Swallow the tablets whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same times every day to keep steady levels in your body.
